title: PAT-ChIP
scope: Illumina PAT-ChIP explanatory schematic: one linear route from FFPE-fixed pathology chromatin through deparaffination/rehydration, MNase digestion, sonication, immunoprecipitation/elution, crosslink reversal/proteinase K digestion and purification to DNA. The separate far-left PAT-ChIP title illustration is descriptive, not an additional operation or branch. The diagram has no library-preparation or sequencing block, no legend assigning chemical identities to colors, and no specified DNA end groups. The card mentions FiT-seq as a distinct refinement, but the supplied abstract does not resolve its operation-by-operation relationship to this route. Downstream library/readout interpretation is limited to DNA recovered by chromatin-target enrichment.

features: Chromatin from formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded pathology tissue; DNA remains associated with chromatin proteins.
The yellow nucleosome drawing at far left captions the assay and is not connected as a separate input or branch.

states.label: Purified DNA
features: Terminal product explicitly labeled DNA; derives from the immunoprecipitated chromatin fraction.

Downstream ChIP-seq uses the recovered DNA sequence to locate genomic regions associated with the selected histone modification or transcription factor. This is a library interface interpretation; library construction and sequencing are not depicted.

A sequencing library would represent the recovered, antibody-enriched DNA fragments, not direct sequencing of histone marks or proteins. Enrichment does not establish perfect target specificity or unbiased recovery.

evidence.rationale: Combined with the figure's immunoprecipitation-to-DNA route and the abstract's ChIP-seq definition, this supports interpreting recovered DNA as the genomic carrier of the selection history. No library chemistry or specificity guarantee follows.

operations.label: Deparaffination and rehydration

operations.mechanism: The card specifies dewaxing with the xylene substitute Histolemon, followed by MNase digestion and sonication; the diagram groups deparaffination and rehydration into one arrow.
operations.information_effect: Changes specimen preparation state while retaining chromatin as the material to be enriched.

operations.label: MNase digestion
operations.description: Digest the DNA component of rehydrated chromatin, producing fragmented chromatin that remains protein-associated and proceeds to sonication.
operations.mechanism: MNase-mediated digestion is explicitly named. The schematic does not specify cleavage sites, DNA end chemistry, or an enzyme concentration.
operations.information_effect: Genomic DNA remains associated with chromatin proteins; the drawing does not establish an exact fragment size or nucleosome count.

operations.label: Sonicate
operations.description: Sonicate the MNase-digested chromatin to obtain the material labeled soluble extract, still containing chromatin protein and DNA.
operations.mechanism: Sonication follows MNase digestion in the depicted route; together they prepare soluble fragmented chromatin.
operations.information_effect: Produces soluble chromatin for immunoprecipitation. The card warns that sonication may introduce sequence bias; neither the figure nor the background yeast study establishes the magnitude of a PAT-ChIP-specific bias.

operations.label: Immunoprecipitate and chromatin elution
operations.description: Enrich a selected fraction of the soluble chromatin by immunoprecipitation and elute that chromatin, yielding protein-associated DNA for crosslink reversal.
operations.mechanism: The immunoprecipitation label and pink antibody-like icon support affinity selection. Capture and elution are retained as the single combined operation shown; support chemistry and antibody specificity are unspecified.
operations.information_effect: Selection enriches DNA fragments associated with the immunoprecipitated chromatin target. The PAT-ChIP abstract supports histone modifications and transcription factor binding as target classes, without identifying the target in this drawing.

operations.label: Reverse crosslink and proteinase K digestion
operations.description: Reverse fixation crosslinks and digest proteins in the eluted chromatin, converting the protein-associated particles into released DNA depicted as a blue line.
operations.mechanism: Crosslink reversal and proteinase K digestion are explicitly grouped under one arrow; the adjacent enzyme-like symbol is an auxiliary reagent icon, not a separate retained material branch.
operations.information_effect: Removes the protein carrier while DNA retains genomic sequence and membership in the selected fraction. The protein or histone modification itself is not the sequenced product.

evidence.rationale: The depicted change from protein-associated DNA to a DNA line indicates removal of the protein association. The retained information is the recovered DNA sequence and its membership in the enriched fraction, rather than physical preservation of the histone mark or protein.

operations.label: Purification
operations.description: Purify the released DNA to produce the terminal material labeled DNA.
operations.information_effect: Supplies selected DNA for downstream ChIP-seq library preparation and genomic readout; the figure does not describe that library preparation.

method_scopes.rationale: All six operations belong to the single workflow captioned pathology tissue chromatin immunoprecipitation (PAT-ChIP). The card identifies FFPE chromatin, Histolemon dewaxing, MNase digestion and sonication; the PAT-ChIP abstract confirms specimen and biological readout. The operation details are schematic claims from the drawing, not full-text protocol verification.
